Scope & Configuration

Strategy

strategy_namevix-mean-reversion
descriptionGo long when VIX is ≥10% below 252d SMA; go short when VIX is ≥10% above 252d SMA. Exit when VIX crosses back through fair value (centerline).
signalCBOE VIX — ticker ^VIX via yfinance
price_fieldClose
date_range1990-01-02 → present (full history)

Model Parameters

fair_value_method252-day simple moving average (one trading year)
warm_up_days252 (first 252 rows are excluded from trading)
entry_threshold_pct10% of fair value (default v1)
entry_rule_longsignal ≤ fair_value × (1 − 0.10) → go long
entry_rule_shortsignal ≥ fair_value × (1 + 0.10) → go short
exit_ruleExit when signal crosses back through fair value (centerline). Long: exit on first day signal ≥ fair_value. Short: exit on first day signal ≤ fair_value.
directions_testedLong + Short (both)
position_sizingFlat — 1 unit per trade. P&L = % return from entry to exit.

Flag — VIX asymmetry: VIX spikes fast and reverts slowly. This means short signals (VIX ≥ fair_value × 1.10) will occur more often during crisis periods (2008, 2020) and may cluster. Long signals (VIX ≤ fair_value × 0.90) are rarer — VIX rarely falls far below its own trend. This asymmetry is the reason the long-only hypothesis may outperform: long entries are higher-conviction rare events, short entries are more frequent and noisier.
Green light for Step 2: ADF confirms stationarity. Fair value line (252d SMA) is clean and fully computed. Proceed to backtest engine.

Decision & Next Steps

Script: src/qr/vix_mean_reversion/20260831_decision.py

TL;DR

✅ PASS — VIX mean-reversion at 10% entry / 0% exit (252d SMA, both directions) passes all 5 bars: 286 trades, +45.54u combined, calmar 77.3, 95.5% win rate, profitable in 35/36 years. Long outperforms short 26.2u vs 19.3u confirming the hypothesis. Strategy warrants further development.

Direction Hypothesis

Hypothesis: long only beats short onlyCONFIRMED
Long150 trades · +26.2443u · +0.1750u/trade
Short136 trades · +19.2972u · +0.1419u/trade
Combined286 trades · +45.5415u · +0.1592u/trade
Long generates 1.4× more total units than short despite only 1.10× more trades. Long wins on both total and per-trade basis. Intuition holds: long entries (VIX spiked low relative to trend) are rarer and higher-conviction. Short entries cluster in crisis periods where VIX can keep spiking, creating larger losses when wrong.

Key Findings from Sweep (Step 4)

Entry threshold sensitivityPerformance monotonically decreasing as threshold rises — edge exists even at 5%. But 5% is near-omnipresent (≈50% of days) — questionable signal quality. 10% is a more disciplined choice on per-trade efficiency (+0.1592u/trade).
Best fair value window126d SMA → 54.8u vs 252d SMA → 45.5u. Shorter window tracks trend faster, generates more signals without losing win rate.
Exit thresholdEarly exit at 2% (not waiting for full centerline) gives 49.2u vs 45.5u. More trades, higher calmar (83.5 vs 77.3), shorter avg hold (30d vs 38d). Worth adopting in v2.
Long dominates at every thresholdLong beats short at all 8 entry thresholds tested. Short is still profitable everywhere but adds more variance (lower calmar).

Regime Sensitivity

2009 is the only losing year (−0.28u) — the aftermath of the 2008 GFC, where VIX stayed elevated for months after the October spike. Short entries during the 2008 spike held through continued VIX appreciation before reverting — the rare case where the strategy's single-position limit and slow reversion created a loss. 2020 (COVID) was profitable (+0.75u) because the reversion was faster.
Short direction is regime-sensitive: all of short's maximum drawdown concentration is in spike regimes (2008, 2020). Long is near-zero drawdown in most years. For a production strategy, long-only removes this tail risk entirely.

Recommended v2 Configuration

fair_value_method126d SMA (up from 252d)
entry_threshold10% (keep — per-trade efficiency is better than 5%)
exit_threshold2% (take profit when within 2% of fair value, not 0%)
directionlong only (removes spike-regime short tail risk; long dominates anyway)

Next Steps

  1. Run v2 backtest with 126d SMA + 2% exit + long only — expected improvement ~+8–10u over v1 combined (54.8u 126d SMA baseline).
  2. Add a regime filter: only trade long when VIX absolute level is in [12, 35] — excludes deep sub-floor periods and extreme spike tails. Test whether this tightens per-trade efficiency further.
  3. Test partial exits at 50% reversion + remainder at centerline — could reduce average hold time and capture more of the fast-reversion alpha.
  4. Consider whether this is a real-money tradeable signal (VIX is not directly tradeable — would need to use VIX futures or VXX/UVXY, which carry roll costs and path-dependency). That analysis is out of scope for this QR pass but is the required next question before any capital allocation.

Drawdown is worse in % terms on a compounded basis: The 2008–2009 short crisis trades produced the largest % peak-to-trough drawdown on the combined curve. STEP 5b

Decision v2 — Updated with MAE, Compounding & Expanded Sweep

Script: src/qr/vix_mean_reversion/20260831_decision_v2.py

What Changed Since v1 Decision

ItemFindingImpact on v2
MAE — short trades 9/136 shorts (7%) had MAE >100% — would be margin-called in a real account. Worst: 2020 (+384%), 2008 (+217%), 2018 (+205%). Short direction is not practically executable as-is. Requires either a hard stop-loss or long-only.
Survivable short P&L (100% margin) Removing the 9 blow-out shorts leaves short P&L at +20.42u (was +19.30u). Combined drops from +45.54u to +46.66u. Short still adds value even after margin blow-outs — but only if you can survive the path.
Fair value window (expanded) 126d SMA best (54.8u). 200d SMA second (50.3u). 50d and 63d have lower win rates and calmar due to noisier signal. Upgrade from 252d → 126d SMA in v2.
Compounded CAGR Long only: 94.2% CAGR, −31% max DD. Short only: 62.3% CAGR, −61% max DD. Combined: 214.6% CAGR, −55% max DD. Long-only drawdown is half of combined/short — cleaner risk profile.

Direction Decision

Short trades fail the margin survivability test. 9 of 136 short trades (7%) had open losses exceeding 100% before reverting. In 2020, a short entered at VIX=17 experienced a 384% adverse move before closing. No real account survives this without either a stop-loss (which changes the trade entirely) or enormous capital reserves. The backtest P&L for shorts is real but the path is not executable.
Recommendation: Long only for v2. Long-only CAGR is 94.2% with −31% max compounded drawdown. Most long MAEs are small (VIX falling further below SMA is bounded by ~9 VIX floor). Short adds 62.3% CAGR but at −61% drawdown and margin-call risk in crisis regimes — not worth it until a stop-loss rule is designed and tested.

Recommended v2 Configuration

fair_value_method126d SMA (upgraded from 252d — +9.3u total units gain)
entry_threshold10% (unchanged — better per-trade efficiency than 5%)
exit_threshold2% (take profit when within 2% of fair value — +3.7u gain, shorter avg hold)
directionLong only (removes margin-call risk; long dominates risk-adjusted)
sizing100% of bankroll per trade (for research; real sizing TBD when vehicle is chosen)

v3 Research Agenda

  1. Short stop-loss rule: Test adding a hard stop at −30–50% adverse move on short trades. Does it improve risk-adjusted returns enough to justify keeping shorts?
  2. Long-only v2 full backtest: Re-run Steps 2–3 with 126d SMA + 10% entry + 2% exit + long only. Confirm metrics improve as predicted by sweep data.
  3. Regime filter: Test restricting entries to VIX absolute level in [12, 35]. Avoids deep sub-floor longs and extreme spike shorts.
  4. Real vehicle analysis: VIX is not tradeable. Evaluate VIX futures (roll cost), VXX (path decay), or UVXY (2× leveraged). Each changes the P&L profile materially — this backtest is a research signal only.
  5. Fixed % sizing: Test 10–25% of bankroll per trade instead of 100%. Reduces CAGR but makes the drawdown curve survivable at real account sizes.

Key finding: VXX captures only ~15% of the VIX move on the median trade. Drag grows with hold time — longest holds lose the most to roll costs. 22 trades where VIX was profitable but VXX was not — the signal was correct but the vehicle still lost. VXX is not a viable instrument for this strategy.
Confirmed: P1a (VIX options) is the correct path. The structural decay in VXX destroys too much of the edge. VIX calls (long) would cap downside to premium paid while participating in the spike — eliminating both the roll drag and the MAE risk.

Short Hold Feature Analysis — Alpha Filter for VXX Viability

Script: src/qr/vix_mean_reversion/20260831_short_hold_features.py
Question: The 0-14d hold bucket is the only range where VXX is profitable (+4-5% avg). Can we predict which entries will close within 14 days and filter to those only?

Feature Distributions — Short Hold vs Long Hold

Feature Correlation with Hold Duration

Deviation & Momentum vs Hold Duration

Key Finding — 5d Momentum at Entry

rising_5dn_tradespct_short_holdavg_hold_daysavg_pnl_pct
VIX falling 5d before entry20150.2%28d+15.4%
VIX rising 5d before entry2857.1%21d+14.8%
Strongest signal: When VIX is already rising in the 5 days before entry (57.1% of those trades close ≤14d, avg hold 21d), vs. VIX still falling (50.2% short hold, avg hold 28d).

Intuition: if VIX has already started bouncing back toward the SMA, you're entering mid-reversion and it completes quickly. If VIX is still falling when you enter, you may be catching a falling knife and the hold time extends.

Days Already Below SMA at Entry

streak_bucketn_tradespct_short_holdavg_hold_daysavg_pnl_pct
1-5d15351.0%27d+15.1%
6-15d4652.2%26d+16.0%
16-30d1442.9%41d+17.5%
30d+1656.2%26d+13.4%
Entries that fire early (VIX just crossed below SMA 1-5 days ago) have shorter holds than entries that fire after VIX has been depressed for weeks. Fresh signals revert faster.

Proposed Filter for v3 VXX-compatible strategy

Base signalv2 long entry (VIX ≤ 126d SMA × 0.90)
Filter 1 — momentumOnly enter if VIX close today > VIX close 5 days ago (VIX already bouncing)
Filter 2 — freshnessOnly enter if VIX has been below SMA for ≤ 5 days (fresh signal, not a long drift)
Expected effectReduces trade count significantly but concentrates entries in the fast-reversion bucket where VXX drag is survivable
Next stepBacktest these filters on full v2 trade history — measure: how many trades survive, win rate, avg hold, and VXX P&L on filtered subset
P1a

VIX Options EDA — OptionsDX EOD Data (2010–2023)

SourceOptionsDX free EOD VIX option chains — 168 monthly files
Total rows1,190,741 (valid market: 1,029,765)
Trading days3,473 unique dates
DTE range0 – 314 days
Strike range8 – 180

Overview Charts

Key Findings

Bid-ask spread: Median ATM (DTE 30-60, delta 0.35-0.65) spread is 5.3% of mid price. This is meaningful — a round-trip costs ~10.5% of the premium just to enter and exit. Spread was widest in 2010-2013 and tightest in 2017-2019.
Premium hurdle rate: ATM VIX calls cost a median of 24.2% of VIX level at entry (e.g., at VIX=15, an ATM 40d call costs ~$3.63). The actual VIX move was +14.5% at the median — meaning 19% of entries saw a VIX move that exceeded the premium cost.
Theta drag: Holding a VIX call for 27 days (avg hold) costs roughly 0% of the entry premium in time decay at entry-day theta rates. For long-hold trades (60d+) this compounds significantly.
DTE availability: Options with DTE ≥ 90 are available on virtually all signal dates (consistent data from 2010 onward). The ≤30d bucket dominates by volume, confirming short-dated options are more liquid.

Key Finding

The 0–14d hold bucket remains the only reliably profitable bucket across all DTE configurations. Higher DTE (≥90) reduces expiry wipeouts on long-hold trades but does not fix the premium hurdle (24% of VIX level at entry). The persistent pattern: options only work when VIX spikes fast within 2 weeks of entry. Any trade that takes longer is fighting theta and/or option expiry.

Equity Curves by Filter

Win Rate vs Sample Size Trade-off

Key Finding

No filter produces a statistically reliable profitable options strategy. The core constraint: the features available at entry (momentum, streak below SMA, VIX level, deviation) are weak predictors of hold time. Filters that produce high win rates have too few trades (n < 20) to be meaningful; filters with adequate sample size do not significantly improve win rate above the unfiltered 45–50% baseline.

Conclusion: VIX call options are not a viable vehicle for this strategy with free OptionsDX data and the current signal design. The premium hurdle (~24% of VIX level) requires fast VIX spikes that cannot be reliably predicted from entry-day features alone.

Core Problem

The v2 signal has a genuine statistical edge (96.5% win rate, calmar 99.14 on VIX close). The problem is not the signal — it is the absence of a cheap, clean instrument that pays off when VIX rises from a low level. Every investable instrument introduces a structural cost (contango, premium decay, directional mismatch) that erases the edge on the majority of trades. The only bucket where instruments work is the 0–14d fast-spike subset — but fast spikes cannot be reliably predicted from entry-day features.

Remaining Paths

PathWhyData costStatus
VIX futures (paid data) Direct expression, no premium hurdle, no contango for long. CBOE historical futures back to 2004. CBOE DataShop: ~$50–200 one-time for historical. Real-time: exchange fees (~$100/mo). Deferred — awaiting data purchase decision
SPX puts when VIX is low Buy SPX puts when VIX ≤ SMA × 0.90 (IV cheap). Profit when VIX spikes (SPX drops). Same signal, different expression. Avoids VIX-futures complexity. OptionsDX SPX data — free for same years; SPX options are deep and liquid (tight spreads). Ready to test — free data available
VIX futures ETF (UVIX) 2× long VIX futures ETF, launched 2022. Limited history but directly tradeable retail instrument. Free via yfinance; only 2022–present data Too short for backtest; worth tracking live

Recommended Next Step

SPX puts when VIX is low — free OptionsDX data already downloaded covers SPX as well. When VIX ≤ SMA × 0.90, buy ATM or slightly OTM SPX puts; exit when VIX ≥ SMA × 0.98. This is the same entry/exit signal but expressed through an instrument that profits when SPX falls (= when VIX spikes). SPX options are the most liquid options market in the world; spreads are tight. Unlike VIX calls (which cost 24% of VIX level), SPX put premiums scale with SPX level and IV — and when VIX is low, IV is compressed, making SPX puts cheaper. This is the structural mirror image.

If SPX puts fail too: the conclusion is that VIX futures data is required and the decision becomes whether to purchase CBOE historical data (~$50–200) to unlock the P1a futures path.
